items.title: Henry A. "Hank" Kmen Interview, 1963-02-13
items.q: And he had, if I recall, practically Joe Marcella playing clarinet with him. ... I never connected that with Joe, my solid clarinet player.

ctx.x: It could be South Rumpal Street Parade or something like that. I can't recall a fan. But what about guys like Perini? Who was he playing with to get along? He was starving to death at the time.

Plenty of us were. That was not unusual at all. There was a little guitar player from this town who's still here now by the name of Clayton Dyrd, I think it's D-U-E-R-R-R, D-E-U-R-R, known as Sunshine. A very fine guitar player. He played with the Joe Venuti Trio a while. And George Hartman from here. There were a whole bunch of people. I don't know how an upstate New York guy who was living and rooming with all these New Orleans fellas, but that's the way it happened. None of us was any too affluent. It was a…
